name: BlackHatWhiteHatRebirth
source:
Dying sucks. Paradoxically, the really violent deaths are often the best sort. Things happen so fast your brain does n't have time to process the signals. *Beep* *Crush* *Splat! * and you are the new hood ornament on a Greyhound Bus. Believe me, I've been there and it hurts. But just for a moment, really. Then your brain gets too overwhelmed with dying that you just sort of go fuzzy and fade out. Yeah, dying's really bad. But it has nothing on rebirth. Rebirth hurts every single time. 
 
 It's like your entire body is on fire when it happens. Except this fire just is n't on the surface, it's everywhere. It's inside you. Every cell in your body is on fire. Except your body is n't really there. You ca n't move. Ca n't scream. Ca n't do anything but burn as some mad violinist draws a hacksaw across your exposed nerves. Then things get worse. A lot worse. It took nine months for you to grow from the size of an eraser tip up being a newborn. It took another 18 years to get to your full size. Try compressing all that into the space of 10 minutes and you'll get a sense of the agony. But you ca n't block it out. You ca n't even black out. You are awake the entire time trying to scream with no lungs to fill. Starving, burning, freezing, thirsty, and drowning all at the same time. Every agony a human can experience, I get them all at once. Yet, I do this over and over again. All because of that White Hat. 
 
 Do n't ask me what my real name is because I do n't even remember it any more. Probably some string of grunts in a language that does n't exist any more. Who knows? I just know that I had a brother. A twin, in fact. For some reason - yet something else I ca n't recall - we absolutely hated each other. We fought over everything. I do n't mean yelling or sibling rivalry. I mean the first time I held a knife to his throat was when we were seven. Probably would have killed him then except he clubbed me over the head with a block of wood. My father broke up the fight later but I think even he knew something was off. Everything about my brother set me off and, apparently, I did the same to him. Whenever we saw each other we tried our best to murder the other. That's what led to us entering the swamp that evening. 
 
 It was the only time my brother and I ever agreed on anything. We knew we could n't do this any more. It had to stop. Neither of us could go on if we knew the other one was living. This was our rite of passage into adulthood. A sort of birthday present from one to the other. Does that sound strange to you? It made sense to us at the time. That night, while our parents slept, we crept out on tiptoes out of the slumbering house. We took our daggers with us and walked into the swamp. I wore a black knitted cap and my brother wore a white knitted cap. We walked for miles into that swamp, until we could no longer see the fires from any of our neighbors, and we faced off in that dank and muddy hole. We screamed and charged at one another. The last thing I saw as I sank into that dark much was my brother's face glaring at me as he sank in front of me. Even as we lay there dying, both the victim of the other's rage, we could n't let it go. The light faded and I experienced my first death but far from my last. 
 
 Every time I die I come back. It's a different time and a different place. I have a new name and a new face. Everything is different. Everything except I always feel compelled to seek out a black hat. I ca n't stop myself. I feel physically ill when I am away from one. I have to wear a hat and it always has to be black. Also, no matter what, eventually I will run across someone wearing a white hat. He will have a face I have never seen before but we always recognize one another and the old rage comes back. Sometimes I kill him. Sometimes he kills me. Always when one of us dies the other ceases to exist immediately afterwards and we are both reborn. 
 
 Over the years I've lead hundreds of lives but only one sort of death. Violent. I've been shot down flying a Sopwith Camel in World War I. I received a bayonet to my spine during the War of 1812. I've been clubbed to death by angry peasants in Medieval Germany and drowned at sea at the hands of a pirate captain. Each time, just before dying, I saw that white hat and knew who had orchestrated my death. Worst of all, he once shot me and my husband while I was still recovering from giving birth to my first child. Oh yes. I am not always a man when I am reborn. I lived for 12 years as a woman that time. After a decade of living of growing up in the 1960s London I dared to think that, perhaps, I had finally been rid of this curse. I allowed a man to court me and we were wed one spring afternoon. Nine months later I gave birth to his child only to look up and see a white hat sitting on a grinning face standing in the doorway. He shot my husband moments before he shot me. 
 
 I think that death is what set me on the path I am now. I know he is coming here tonight. I saw him in the crowd at the market today. That white hat bobbing above the top of the crowd. I did n't see the face. I did n't have to. The moment I spied the hat that familiar bestial rage swelled up inside of me. He had found me once again! 
 
 So, tonight, I wait for him here in my basement. This soundproof basement in my cabin so far out here all alone. 
 
 The front door is unlocked. He can walk right in with his sword drawn or his gun before him. It does n't matter. He will come for me. He wo n't be able to resist the siren song. It is in our blood. It pounds in our ears. I can hear its drums beating even now. He will come for me. He will search for me and he will come down those dark steps to find me. Oh yes he will. So dark he will never spy that trip wire until it is too late. The contact plate at the bottom of the stairs will wait for him. But, do n't worry dear brother. The voltage is low. It wo n't kill you. You wo n't die at my hands like so many times before. It will just incapacitate you for a moment. Just a few moments as I get the chains in place. Just long enough for the hammer to strike and splinter your bones in your arms and legs. 
 
 Yes, dear brother. This time it is different. This time I am going to live and I ca n't do that without you.
retelling:
From the Perspective of The White Hat:

In an endless cycle of life and death, I find myself consistently pursued by my twin brother, the one who wears a black hat. Our enmity, as old as time itself, has driven us through countless reincarnations, each more violent than the last.

I am known to others by many names, but in this narrative, I am simply The White Hat. My twin's alteration of hat color serves as a stark reminder of our eternal conflict, a symbol of our unyielding hatred that spans across time and space.

The swamp was where it all began, the place we first shed blood, our initial act of mutual destruction. The darkness, the mud, the dampness - I can still feel the weight of those memories in the marshy ground beneath my boots. Yet, each death is not the end, but the beginning of another life, a new identity, and a fresh setting.

In one life, I soared through the skies over battlefields during World War I, piloting a Sopwith Camel. In another, I fought as a foot soldier in the War of 1812. I've lived many lives - a pirate, a peasant, even a woman in 1960s London. Each existence is filled with the anticipation of our inevitable encounter, always ending in our shared demise.

This time, however, my twin has prepared differently. The present finds us in a remote cabin's basement, where they have set up a trap to capture me rather than kill me. I sense an undercurrent of hope, a desire to end this cycle that plagues us both. But can our unquenchable hatred truly be quelled? As the game of cat and mouse continues, I cannot help but wonder if we are destined to repeat this cycle for eternity.
